intro: Impact, effort and dependency for each. Nothing is built until you choose it; items marked implemented were requested outright in the brief.

items.title: Promote one canonical data set and archive the rest
items.why: Six folders publish the same series with different labels; a reader can act on a row another folder marks unverified. One source removes the contradiction.
items.not_implemented: Nothing was moved or deleted in this session.

items.title: Store the room's written answer, then let labels flip automatically
items.why: Q1 is the real blocker. A per-event rules_confirmed object holding the quote, date and channel lets the badge change itself and shows what justified it.

items.title: Extend the rate log to full checkout totals
items.why: Rate + fee + tax is still not what you pay. The log already reserves fields for checkout_total, nightly_average, mandatory_fee, tax, parking, cancellation_deadline and rate_timestamp, so like-for-like comparison becomes a query.

items.title: Parse other rooms' daily schedules into the same schema
items.why: Once a Wynn or Bellagio page parses, the same rule audit and overlap check apply, and the plan stops being single-property.

items.title: Make the walk check a stored, dated observation
items.why: Minutes change with construction and entry point. A dated observation with the route link is auditable; a remembered number is not.

items.title: Write the verification policy on the board and enforce it in CI
items.why: Most irregularities in this repo came from sessions calling a row verified on inference. One policy line plus a verifier gate makes it structural.

items.title: Add a change-triage view listing only rows whose source moved
items.why: A daily re-check is noise unless changed rows surface in one place with before/after quotes; the state file already stores hashes and change dates.

items.title: Rank on money actually entering the pool, not the advertised buy-in
items.why: The sheets show the fee is withheld FROM the buy-in ($58 of $300 to the house, $242 to the pool) and some flights discount the fee for early registration, so pool-per-entry is the comparable figure.
items.status: partly implemented: column shown; ranking still gated on Q1

items.title: Keep a 'do not book yet' banner until Q1 and Q2 close
items.why: The biggest risk is paying for a trip on a plan that assumed freezeout play. The banner is the cheapest control.

items.title: Record actual field sizes after each event
items.why: Guarantee/entry is descriptive; entries actually recorded is the number that matters. Post-event counts turn the ratio into evidence across a series.

items.title: Fail loudly when an official page stops being readable
items.why: The Wynn page returned the home page twice. Storing final URL, title and byte count turns 'no data' into a visible problem instead of a silently stale row.

items.title: Keep bounty, satellite, seniors, ladies and other-game events out of the ranking
items.why: The brief asks for them in a separate section; it also stops a $8,000 pool that includes bounties from being compared with a plain $10,000 pool.
